english: Not ivory nor golden
note: Negatives kept in place: non ... neque (lines 1, 3, 5, 7).

english: in my house gleams a panelled ceiling,
note: lacunar: a coffered (panelled) ceiling; renidet: gleams, shines back.

english: not Hymettian beams
note: trabes Hymettiae: architraves (lit. beams) of marble from Mount Hymettus near Athens.

english: press columns cut in farthest
note: ultima ... Africa (lines 4-5): ablative, 'in farthest Africa'; the columns are of Numidian marble quarried there.

english: Africa, nor, of Attalus
an unknown heir, the palace have I seized,
note: Attalus III of Pergamum bequeathed his kingdom to Rome; ignotus heres: an heir no one knew of (unsuspected). occupavi: perfect, 'have I taken possession of'.

english: nor Laconian, for me,
do honourable client-women draw purples.
note: trahunt: draw (out the wool), i.e. spin; purpuras: purple (Laconian-dyed) wools or garments; clientae: feminine, the wives of clients; honestae: of good standing.

english: But good faith and, of talent,
note: ingeni: genitive of ingenium (talent, wit).

english: a kindly vein is (there), and, poor, the rich man
note: vena: vein (of ore), metaphor for a rich source of talent. est: 'there is'. pauperem agrees with me (line 11): 'me, poor though I am'.

english: seeks me: nothing beyond
note: petit: seeks out, courts.

english: the gods do I importune, nor a powerful friend
note: supra deos: beyond what the gods give. lacesso: provoke, importune. amicum: Maecenas.

english: for more lavish things do I demand,
note: flagito takes a double accusative: the friend (line 12) and largiora.

english: enough blessed with my only Sabines.
note: unicis Sabinis: lit. 'the only Sabines', i.e. his single Sabine estate (the farm Maecenas gave him); 'my' supplied.

english: Day is thrust on by day,
and new moons go on to perish:
note: pergunt interire: proceed to die, i.e. wane.

english: you marbles to be cut
note: secanda: gerundive, 'to be sawn' (into slabs).

latin: locas sub ipsum funus et sepulcri
english: put out on contract close upon the very funeral, and, of the tomb
note: sub ipsum funus: on the eve of death; sepulcri goes with line 19

english: unmindful, you build houses,
note: struis domos: builds houses (not a tomb).

english: and, of the sea roaring at Baiae, you press
note: Bais: at (or against) Baiae, the resort on the Bay of Naples; obstrepentis agrees with maris. urges: press on, strive.

english: to push back the shores,
note: submovere litora: building villas out on piers into the sea.

english: too little rich with the containing bank;
note: continente ripa: ablative, 'with the mainland shore' (lit. the bank that holds you in); parum locuples: not rich enough.

english: What of the fact that continually the nearest
note: quid quod: 'what (of the fact) that'.

english: you tear up, of the field, boundary-stones, and beyond
note: terminos: boundary-stones, sacred to Terminus.

english: the borders of your clients
note: 'your' supplied.

english: you leap, greedy? There is driven out, ancestral
note: salis: from salio, you leap (over). pellitur: singular verb with the two subjects in line 28.

english: in the fold of the garment carrying gods,
note: sinu: the fold of the garment at the breast; paternos ... deos: the ancestral household gods. ferens: singular.

latin: et uxor et vir sordidosque natos.
english: both wife and husband, and squalid children.
note: sordidos: dirty, ragged.

english: No more certain, however,
note: nulla ... aula (line 31): 'no hall'.

english: than of rapacious Orcus the boundary, appointed,
note: fine: ablative of comparison with certior; destinata agrees with aula (line 31). Orcus: the underworld, or its god. Text: Shorey reads fine destinata; some editors read sede destinata.

english: hall awaits the rich
note: divitem ... erum (32): 'the rich master'.

latin: erum. quid ultra tendis? aequa tellus
english: master. Why further do you strain? Impartial earth
note: tendis: stretch, strive. aequa: equal, impartial.

english: for the poor man is opened
and for kings' boys; nor the attendant of Orcus
note: satelles Orci: Charon (or Mercury), the ferryman/escort of the dead. pueris: boys, sons.

english: cunning Prometheus
note: Promethea: Greek accusative.

english: brought back, by gold captured; he the proud
note: revexit: carried back (from the underworld). Some manuscripts read revinxit ('unbound'); Shorey prints revexit. captus: won over (bribed). hic: Orcus.

english: Tantalus, and of Tantalus
the stock restrains; he, to relieve, having done
note: coercet: confines, holds in check. functum ... laboribus: 'having discharged his labours' (fungor with ablative).

english: the poor man, with labours,
note: laboribus goes with functum (line 38).

english: called and not called hears.
note: audit: hears, i.e. heeds (the prayer to be released).

english: Bacchus among remote, songs, rocks
note: in remotis ... rupibus: 'among remote rocks'; carmina: object of docentem (line 2).

english: I saw teaching, believe me, posterity,
note: credite posteri: 'believe (it), you of later times'; 'me' supplied.

english: and Nymphs learning, and the ears
note: discentis: accusative plural (-is for -es).

english: of goat-footed Satyrs, pointed.
note: auris ... acutas: pricked-up (pointed) ears; auris = aures.

english: Euhoe! With fresh fear my mind trembles,
note: euhoe: Bacchic cry, kept as in the Latin. 'my' supplied.

english: and, with a breast full of Bacchus, turbulently
note: turbidum: accusative neuter used adverbially, 'in turmoil'.

english: it rejoices. Euhoe, spare, Liber,
note: Liber: Bacchus.

english: spare, you to be feared for the heavy thyrsus.
note: metuende: vocative gerundive, 'you who are to be feared'; gravi ... thyrso: ablative, 'for (or with) the heavy thyrsus', the ivy-wreathed staff.

english: Right it is for me the persistent Thyiads
note: fas est: it is permitted (divinely). Thyiadas: Greek accusative plural, the Bacchants; pervicacis = pervicaces, unwearying.

english: and the fountain of wine, and of milk the rich
to sing, streams, and from trunks
note: cantare governs Thyiadas, fontem, rivos. truncis ... cavis (12): from hollow trunks.

english: hollow fallen, to tell again, the honeys;
note: lapsa ... mella: honeys that have dripped. iterare: repeat, retell.

english: right also, of the blessed wife added
note: beatae coniugis: Ariadne, wife of Bacchus, whose crown was set among the stars.

english: to the stars, the honour, and the roofs of Pentheus
note: Penthei: genitive of Pentheus (Greek name); Pentheus of Thebes resisted Bacchus and his palace was overthrown.

english: scattered with not gentle ruin,
note: non leni: negative kept as it stands ('not gentle').

english: and, of Thracian, the destruction, of Lycurgus.
note: Thracis ... Lycurgi: 'of Thracian Lycurgus', king of the Edoni who persecuted Bacchus.

latin: tu flectis amnis, tu mare barbarum,
english: You bend rivers, you the barbarian sea,
note: flectis governs both objects; the sea is the Indian Ocean (Bacchus' conquest of India).

english: you, on separate ridges, drenched,
note: uvidus: wet, i.e. drenched with wine; separatis ... iugis: remote ridges.

english: with a knot restrain viperine
note: nodo ... viperino: with a knot of vipers.

english: of the Bistonian women, without harm, the hair.
note: Bistonidum: genitive plural, Thracian (Bistonian) Bacchants. sine fraude: without harm (to them). crinis = crines, accusative.

latin: tu, cum parentis regna per arduum
english: You, when, of your father, the realms, by the steep,
note: parentis: Jupiter; 'your' supplied. per arduum: up the steep way.

english: the band of Giants was climbing, impious,
note: scanderet: imperfect subjunctive with cum; inpia agrees with cohors.

english: Rhoetus you hurled back, with the lion's
note: Rhoetus: one of the Giants. Bacchus fought in lion form.

english: claws and dreadful jaw;
note: mala: ablative singular of mala, jaw.

english: although for dances fitter and jests
and play said, not enough suited
note: dictus: having been called; non sat: 'not enough', negative kept.

english: for fight, you were reputed; but the same
note: ferebaris: you were said, reputed. idem: the same (you).

english: of peace you were, and the middle, of war.
note: medius: the mid-point, i.e. you were the same (you) both in peace and in the midst of war; pacis and belli both depend on medius.

english: Cerberus, harmless, saw you, with golden
note: te is object, Cerberus subject: Cerberus saw you. insons: unharming, innocent (made gentle).

english: horn adorned, gently rubbing
note: decorum agrees with te: you adorned with the golden horn. atterens: rubbing (against you) his tail.

english: his tail, and, departing, with three-tongued
note: recedentis: genitive, 'of (you) departing', with pedes (line 32). 'his' supplied.

english: mouth the feet, and touched the legs.
note: pedes ... crura: your feet and legs (licked them).

english: Not on an ordinary nor a slender shall I be borne
note: non ... nec: negatives kept in place. ferar: future passive.

english: wing, two-formed, through the liquid air
note: penna: wing (lit. feather). biformis: of two forms, man and bird (also poet). aethera: Greek accusative, the upper air.

english: bard, nor on the earth shall I delay
note: vates: poet-prophet.

english: longer, and, than envy greater,
note: invidia: ablative of comparison.

english: cities shall I leave. Not I, of poor
note: urbis = urbes, accusative plural.

latin: sanguis parentum, non ego, quem vocas.
english: blood of parents, not I, whom you call.
note: sanguis: offspring. quem vocas: 'whom you call (to you)', or 'whom you call (dear)'; Shorey's text has a full stop here, which is kept, but the sense runs on into the vocative of line 7.

english: beloved Maecenas, shall die
note: obibo: shall go to death, perish.

english: nor by the Stygian wave shall I be held.
note: Stygia ... unda: by the wave of the Styx.

english: Already, already settle on my legs rough
note: residunt: settle, sink in. cruribus: dative/ablative, 'on the shins'; 'my' supplied.

latin: pelles et album mutor in alitem
english: skins, and into a white I am changed bird
note: album ... alitem: a white bird (the swan).

english: above, and there spring up smooth
note: superne: on the upper parts.

english: over fingers and shoulders feathers.
Already, than Daedalean Icarus better known,
note: notior: Shorey's reading; many editors read ocior, 'swifter'. Daedaleo: son of Daedalus.

english: I shall visit the shores of groaning Bosporus
note: gementis ... Bospori: 'of the groaning Bosporus'.

english: and the Gaetulian Syrtes, tuneful
note: Syrtis = Syrtes, the shoals off North Africa; Gaetulian = African.

english: bird, and Hyperborean plains.
note: Hyperboreos: of the far North.

latin: me Colchus et qui dissimulat metum
english: Me the Colchian, and who hides fear
note: qui dissimulat metum: the Dacian who hides (pretends not to have) fear.

english: of the Marsian cohort, the Dacian, and the farthest
note: Marsae cohortis: the Marsian troops, the best Roman infantry.

english: Geloni shall know; me the skilled
note: Geloni: Scythian tribe.

english: shall learn, the Iberian, and of the Rhone the drinker.
note: peritus Hiber: the learned Spaniard; Rhodani potor: the Gaul.

english: Let be absent from my empty funeral dirges
note: inani funere: the funeral is empty (there is no body); 'my' supplied. neniae: dirges.

english: and unseemly mournings and laments;
check the outcry, and of the tomb
omit the superfluous honours.
note: mitte: let go, omit.

english: I hate the uninitiated crowd and keep it off.
note: profanum: outside the shrine, uninitiated. arceo: keep away; 'it' supplied.

english: Be favourable with tongues: songs not before
note: favete linguis: ritual formula, 'speak words of good omen', i.e. keep holy silence.

english: heard, of the Muses the priest,
for maidens and boys I sing.
Of kings to be feared over their own flocks
note: Sense: the command of dreaded kings is over their own flocks (the verb est is in line 6); 'their' renders proprios.

latin: reges in ipsos imperium est Iovis,
english: over kings themselves the command is of Jove,
note: Iovis: of Jupiter.

english: famous for the Giant triumph,
note: Giganteo triumpho: the triumph over the Giants.

english: all things with an eyebrow moving.
note: supercilio: by his brow (nod).

latin: est ut viro vir latius ordinet
english: It is (so) that man than man more widely arranges
note: est ut: it may be that. viro: dative/ablative of comparison 'than (another) man'.

english: plantations in furrows, this one more nobly born
note: arbusta: tree-plantings (trees for training vines). sulcis: in furrows (trenches).

english: goes down into the Field as candidate,
note: campum: the Campus Martius, where elections were held. descendat: subjunctive after est ut.

english: in morals this one and better in repute
note: moribus ... fama: ablative of respect.

english: contends, for that one the crowd of clients
note: contendat: subjunctive (after est ut). illi: dative.

english: is greater: by equal law Necessity
note: sit: subjunctive. Necessitas: personified.

english: allots the distinguished and the lowest;
note: sortitur: draws lots for, assigns by lot; insignis = insignes.

english: the roomy urn shakes every name.
note: omne ... nomen is object, urna subject: the capacious urn shakes every name (lots in the urn).

english: Drawn sword for whom above the impious
note: cui: the man over whose impious neck the drawn sword hangs (Damocles). destrictus: unsheathed.

english: neck hangs, not Sicilian feasts
note: Siculae dapes: the proverbial luxury of the Syracusan tyrants.

english: a sweet flavour will work out,
note: elaborabunt: will produce with effort.

english: not of birds and of the lyre the singing
note: avium: of birds (in aviaries).

english: sleep will bring back: sleep, of rustic
note: Negatives in lines 18 and 20 kept in place.

english: gentle, men, not humble houses
note: agrestium ... virorum: of countrymen; non humilis domos: not the humble houses (it does not disdain them).

english: disdains, and the shady bank,
note: fastidit: disdains; non (line 22, line 24) negates it.

english: not Tempe stirred by Zephyrs.
note: Tempe: Greek neuter plural, the valley in Thessaly; Zephyris: by west winds. 'not' repeats from line 22: (does not disdain) Tempe.

english: The one desiring what is enough neither
note: desiderantem: accusative, object of sollicitat (line 26).

english: does the tumultuous sea trouble
note: sollicitat: troubles, disturbs; subject mare.

english: nor the savage, of Arcturus setting,
note: Arcturi cadentis: the setting of Arcturus (late October), stormy season.

english: onset, or of the rising Kid,
note: Haedi: the Kid, a star rising in early October, also a storm-sign.

english: not lashed by hail vineyards
and the farm, lying, the tree now the waters
note: fundus mendax: a deceitful farm (failing its promise). arbore: ablative absolute with culpante (line 31), 'the tree blaming'.

english: blaming, now scorching the fields
note: torrentia agros: torrentia is the participle agreeing with sidera (line 32).

english: stars, now winters unfair.
note: Construction (lines 29-32): the troubles listed do not trouble (sollicitat, line 26) the man content with enough.

english: The fish feel the waters narrowed
note: The fish (subject) feel the waters (object) narrowed.

latin: iactis in altum molibus: huc frequens
english: by masses thrown into the deep: hither thronging
note: molibus: masses, piles (foundations of seaside villas). frequens: in numbers, with a crowd.

english: rubble lets down the contractor
note: caementa: rough stones for concrete. redemptor: the building contractor.

english: with servants, and the master, of land
note: terrae ... fastidiosus: weary of (scorning) land.

english: disdainful: but Fear and Threats
note: Timor, Minae: personified.

english: climb to the same place where the master (does), nor
note: eodem, quo: to the same place to which.

english: withdraws from the bronze-beaked trireme, and
note: aerata: bronze-fitted (beaked).

english: behind the horseman sits black Care.
note: Cura: Care, personified.

english: But if the one grieving neither Phrygian stone
note: Phrygius lapis: Phrygian (Synnadic) marble. dolentem: object of delenit (line 43).

english: nor, of purples than a star brighter,
note: purpurarum ... usus: the use (wearing) of purple garments brighter than a star.

english: soothes, the use, nor Falernian
vine and Achaemenian costus,
note: Achaemenium: Persian. costum: costus, an aromatic perfume (unguent).

english: why, with doorposts to be envied and in new
note: invidendis: gerundive, to be envied.

english: lofty fashion should I build up an atrium?
note: sublime: lofty, agreeing with atrium. moliar: deliberative subjunctive.

english: Why for the valley should I exchange Sabine
note: valle ... Sabina: ablative of exchange, for my Sabine valley.

english: riches more laborious?
note: operosiores: more troublesome (requiring more toil).

english: Narrow, as a friend, poverty to endure
note: amice: adverb, in friendly fashion (gladly). Some editors read amici; Shorey prints amice.

english: sturdy, in harsh soldiering, a boy
note: militia: ablative, in military service.

english: let learn thoroughly, and the Parthians fierce
note: condiscat: jussive subjunctive. ferocis = feroces.

english: let him harass, a horseman to be feared with spear,
note: vexet: jussive. metuendus: gerundive.

latin: vitamque sub divo et trepidis agat
english: and life under the open sky and in anxious let him spend
note: sub divo: under the sky, in the open air. trepidis ... in rebus: amid dangers.

latin: in rebus. illum ex moenibus hosticis
english: affairs. Him from the walls of the enemy
note: hosticis: hostile, of the enemy.

english: the matron of the warring tyrant
note: matrona: the wife of the enemy king.

english: looking out, and the grown maiden,
note: adulta virgo: the marriageable daughter.

english: may sigh: "alas, lest the unskilled in battle-lines
note: Quotation marks as in the Latin source. ne ... lacessat: 'lest (he) provoke' (fear clause). rudis agminum: unpractised in battle-columns.

english: betrothed provoke, royal, the rough
note: sponsus regius: the royal betrothed.

english: to touch, lion, whom bloody
note: asperum tactu: rough to touch (dangerous to handle); leonem: the Roman youth as lion.

english: through the midst of slaughters sweeps wrath."
note: rapit: snatches, carries headlong. Closing quotation mark as in the Latin source.

latin: dulce et decorum est pro patria mori:
english: Sweet and fitting it is for fatherland to die:
note: decorum: seemly, fitting.

english: death also pursues the fleeing man
note: mors (subject) pursues the fleeing man (object): fugacem ... virum.

english: nor spares, of unwarlike youth,
note: inbellis iuventae: genitive with poplitibus (line 16).

english: the hamstrings and the timid back.
note: poplitibus: the backs of the knees (dative with parcit).

english: Virtue, of defeat ignorant, sordid,
note: repulsae ... sordidae: of base electoral rebuff (repulsa = defeat at the polls); Virtus: personified.

english: with unstained honours shines
note: intaminatis ... honoribus: with untainted offices (honours).

english: nor takes up or lays down the axes
note: securis = secures, the axes of the fasces, emblems of office.

english: at the decision of the popular breeze.
note: aurae: breeze, i.e. popular favour.

english: Virtue, opening to the undeserving to die
note: inmeritis mori: to those not deserving to die.

english: heaven, by a denied way tries a journey,
note: negata ... via: by a way refused (to others).

english: and gatherings common and the damp
note: coetus: assemblies, crowds.

english: spurns the ground with fleeing wing.
note: penna: wing (lit. feather).

english: There is also for faithful, safe, silence
note: fideli ... silentio: for loyal silence; tuta: safe, agreeing with merces.

english: a reward: I shall forbid that he who, of Ceres, the rite
note: vetabo ... sit / solvat: I shall forbid that he be / unmoor. Cereris sacrum: the mysteries of Ceres (Eleusinian).

english: has divulged, secret, under the same
note: volgarit = volgaverit, perfect subjunctive. arcanae agrees with Cereris: 'of secret Ceres'.

english: be beams, and the fragile with me
note: trabibus: roof-beams; sit: subjunctive after vetabo.

english: unmoor the bean-boat; often Diespiter,
note: phaselon: Greek accusative of phaselus, a light boat (lit. 'bean-pod'). Diespiter: Jupiter (old form).

english: neglected, to the impure has added the pure;
note: incesto ... integrum: has joined the innocent with the guilty (in punishment).

english: rarely the one going ahead, wicked,
note: antecedentem scelestum: the criminal running ahead.

english: has abandoned, with foot, Punishment, lame.
note: pede ... claudo: with lame foot; Poena: Punishment, personified. addidit, deseruit: gnomic perfects.
